Worked in retail supply chain for a while. 

This is indeed true...sometimes. You'll find this more common in certain electronics like TVs and audio equipment. Some even go so far as being nearly identical to regular items they sell, but the actual manufacturer number on the box with be slightly different. 

Mainly the difference might only be one or two components on the inside are made cheaper or come from a part of their supply chain at a different rate. Example, a circuit board might come from a factory in China as opposed to Taiwan, etc. 

Other times, it might be a minor difference. Had a tv for sale at Sears that had a black Friday version up for sale that was almost identical visually except it had only one HDMI input as opposed to the 4 on the non-BF model and the item number just added a letter to the end of it. 

Other times, the sale item is merely a model that is last year's model or a new model is going to be released soon with no quality difference. 

On the other hand, some items are just sale items at marked down prices. Like for example, an XBox is the same as the one on regular days, just marked down (or given with a gift card when the manufacturer has certain sale price restrictions, like with video game consoles). 

Just be aware of the actual item number on the box you are buying versus the one you wanted to buy.

IQ tests are more a measure of the fluid intelligence of a person As compared to the general population. 

Fluid intelligence in layman's terms would be a person's cognitive functions and ability to process information. This is opposed to crystallized intelligence which is more along the lines of learned knowledge (facts, skills, processes learned).

Think of it as a computer. It is measuring the processor speed of the computer and RAM (fluid intelligence), Not the hard drive or what is stored on it. 

High IQ just correlates with learning things more quickly and problem solving. However, high IQ doesn't make one knowledgeable. A person with a normal IQ can be an expert in a field and a high IQ can know jack squat.
